purpose: Etail review refinements informed by publicly disclosed Amex architecture. Separate from the frozen 90-task product comparison; not an implementation or private-architecture similarity score.

gates.title: Command identity and scope
gates.acceptance: Use stable business-command identity bound to account, resource, command type and payload. Duplicate identical submissions return the same result; an identity reused with different scope or payload is rejected. Concurrent requests produce one authorized business effect.

gates.title: Uncertain provider outcome
gates.acceptance: A mock provider accepts an issuance then loses its response. Retrying and reconciling produces one card and the same provider correlation. UI and operator queue retain a truthful pending/uncertain state until an authoritative result; no invented completion.

gates.title: Effect and acknowledgement crash
gates.acceptance: Kill the worker after a durable effect but before acknowledgement. Recovery reuses the business identity, records the received result once and never posts a second journal. Faults before dispatch, during dispatch and after confirmation have separate expected outcomes.

gates.title: Atomic money and control authority
gates.acceptance: Concurrent spend, backing change and limit revision obey one committed order; no overspending or unsupported capacity. All amounts remain exact and currency-qualified. Delayed analytics/CRM projections cannot authorize a financial effect.

gates.title: Audit versus diagnostics
gates.acceptance: A diagnostic-sink outage does not duplicate or incorrectly reject a valid mock effect and is operationally visible. Failure to persist mandatory financial/audit evidence prevents success. Diagnostic buffering never substitutes for the immutable journal or required audit trail.

gates.title: Reference-data effective versions
gates.acceptance: A calculation records the applicable reference/rule version and effective time. Replaying under that version reproduces the result. Stale or absent required data produces an explicit defined outcome; it never silently guesses a rate or cost.

gates.title: Side-effect-disabled replay
gates.acceptance: Replay fictional scenarios through the same policy/handlers to compare a candidate change. Assert no provider call, posted money, email or other external effect escapes the harness. Replays do not use legacy source, databases or customer traffic.

gates.title: Failure and load regression
gates.acceptance: For the exact implementation SHA, exercise bounded bursts, duplicate/out-of-order events, dependency timeout and recovery. Record correctness plus p95/p99 latency, backlog age and resource usage. Thresholds require an explicit Etail baseline; no Amex benchmark is reused as an Etail SLA.

gates.title: Reconciliation chain
gates.acceptance: Trace one fictional purchase across command, provider event, hold/capture, journal, account projection and merchant settlement. Exercise partial clearing, reversal, refund and duplicate events. Operator corrections use scoped common commands with an attributable audit.

gates.title: Recovery authority and user visibility
gates.acceptance: Every unresolved financial state has a responsible queue and next permitted action. A viewer cannot retry or adjust; authorized recovery cannot bypass account scope. Consumer/merchant views explain status and permitted next steps without exposing private operator data.

gates.title: Rollout and restoration proof
gates.acceptance: Before hosted release, rehearse restoration and rollback with exact schema/config/application versions and persisted financial fixtures. Code rollback must not reverse completed external effects or edit posted journals. Record data compatibility and unresolved-result reconciliation.

gates.title: Evidence and component boundaries
gates.acceptance: Any architecture/dependency proposal identifies the actual Amex subsystem, source date, evidence class and Etail need. A historical approval, conference logo, job posting, patent or repository is not upgraded to current deployment proof. No second policy, issuance or ledger owner is introduced.
